root_cause.text: In the Xilinx axienet TX cleanup path, BQL accounting used per-descriptor `ACTUAL_LEN` from `axienet_free_tx_chain()` and reset the accumulator every NAPI poll, so scatter-gather packets whose BDs completed across polls lost already-freed bytes and were never credited back to BQL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `axienet_free_tx_chain()` to add `cur_p->skb->len` only when the last BD of a packet completes (`if (cur_p->skb && (status & ...COMPLETE_MASK))`) and removes the old `*sizep += status & XAXIDMA_BD_STS_ACTUAL_LEN_MASK;` logic; the commit message explicitly says the previous per-BD sum was “reset on each NAPI poll” and that “earlier bytes are lost and never credited to BQL,” causing the TX queue to stall.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the documentation for the transmit cleanup byte-count accumulator to match its actual packet-length semantics.
intent_record.what: The kernel-doc comment for the @sizep parameter was updated: it now says the pointed-to u32 accumulates the total byte count of completed packets using skb->len, instead of describing it as the sum of all bytes in cleaned-up descriptors.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior in the code shown; it only clarifies the intended meaning of the sizep output value so readers understand it tracks completed packet lengths rather than raw descriptor bytes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TX completion accounting by adding skb length to the optional size accumulator when freeing completed descriptors.
intent_record.what: Inside axienet_free_tx_chain(), in the branch that handles a completed TX buffer descriptor with an associated skb, two new lines were added to conditionally accumulate the skb length into *sizep when sizep is non-NULL, before calling napi_consume_skb().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now tracks the total number of transmitted bytes for completed packets when the caller supplies a size accumulator pointer. This preserves byte accounting for TX completion processing without changing skb reclamation or packet counting behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the TX descriptor length accumulation from axienet_free_tx_chain() so it no longer updates the optional size output while freeing descriptors.
intent_record.what: The code block inside axienet_free_tx_chain() no longer conditionally increments *sizep by the descriptor's actual length; the three lines checking sizep and adding status & XAXIDMA_BD_STS_ACTUAL_LEN_MASK were removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will stop accumulating transmitted byte counts into the optional sizep output while freeing TX descriptors, so callers will no longer receive a total size computed from the freed chain.

grouping_result.intent: Clarify the documentation for the transmit cleanup byte-count accumulator to match its actual packet-length semantics.
Fix TX completion accounting by adding skb length to the optional size accumulator when freeing completed descriptors.
Remove the TX descriptor length accumulation from axienet_free_tx_chain() so it no longer updates the optional size output while freeing descriptors.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly targets the TX cleanup byte-count accumulator semantics, which are central to the BQL accounting bug described in the root cause. Even though it is a documentation clarification, it is directly about the flawed accumulator behavior.

The root cause is incorrect BQL/TX cleanup accounting for completed scatter-gather descriptors. This change directly fixes TX completion accounting by accumulating skb length when freeing descriptors, which addresses the same accounting bug.

The change directly modifies axienet_free_tx_chain(), which is the function involved in the BQL accounting bug. Removing the per-descriptor length accumulation affects how freed TX bytes are reported, matching the root cause around incorrect size accounting across NAPI polls.

candidates.rationale: This conditional enables the buggy per-descriptor byte accumulation path. When sizep is provided, the cleanup code updates the byte counter for each completed BD, which is the mechanism that causes already-freed bytes to be accounted inconsistently across NAPI polls.

This is the directly vulnerable statement: it adds only the current descriptor's ACTUAL_LEN to the accumulator during TX cleanup. Because the accumulator is reset each NAPI poll, scatter-gather packets whose descriptors complete across polls lose previously freed bytes and are never fully credited back to BQL.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line performs the per-descriptor TX byte accumulation in axienet_free_tx_chain(). Because the accumulator is reset every NAPI poll, scatter-gather packets completed across multiple polls lose already-freed bytes and are not fully credited back to BQL.

This conditional enables the buggy byte-accounting path by allowing axienet_free_tx_chain() to update the optional size output during descriptor cleanup. That mechanism is what caused inconsistent BQL accounting across NAPI polls.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version. The shown code has already been refactored to accumulate completion accounting across all cleaned descriptors in one call: `packets = axienet_free_tx_chain(ndev, lp->tx_bd_ci, -1, &size);` and then `ndev->stats.tx_bytes += size;`. Inside `axienet_free_tx_chain()`, bytes are added for each completed descriptor via `if (sizep) *sizep += status & XAXIDMA_BD_STS_ACTUAL_LEN_MASK;`, and there is no reset of the byte accumulator within this TX cleanup path. This means the specific bug described—using per-descriptor `ACTUAL_LEN` but resetting the accumulator every NAPI poll so bytes completed across polls were lost—is not visible here. Since the fix is already present in this commit, `is_fixed` is YES and `has_bug` is NO.
